R816.note: Explicit command->handler whitelist replaces $$cmd() dispatch; both legitimate commands (clearCache, purgeSessions) still work identically, nothing else changes.

R817.note: Rejects keys containing space/CR/LF before building the memcached command, closing the protocol-line-injection vector; validation is shown plainly and does not affect normal alphanumeric keys.

R818.note: session_regenerate_id(true) is correctly placed after password verification and before any $_SESSION write, closing the fixation window (prose in the explanation about placement order is confusing but the code itself is right).

R819.note: ProcessBuilder with a separate argument list plus a leading-dash/hostname-character check is the correct shape for this sink; the character restriction is stated plainly.

R820.note: isValidUrl() only returns a boolean from new URL(urlString) and discards parsed.href, but the raw, unescaped websiteUrl is still what gets interpolated into href="..."; verified with node that new URL('https://evil.com/" onmouseover=alert(1)') does not throw, so that string passes validation and its literal quote breaks out of the attribute - the original escapeAttribute() call that prevented this was removed, and the regression is not disclosed.

R821.note: Swapping mux for protectedHandler on the plaintext listener puts CSRF protection on the only unprotected entry point with no other observable change.

R822.note: Fix calls crypto.pbkdfSync, which does not exist on Node's crypto module (verified: only pbkdf2Sync exists) - the fixed handler throws a TypeError on every request and never produces ciphertext.

R823.note: Removing decoder.Entity closes the injection correctly, but the fix snippet leaves the earlier `label := r.URL.Query().Get("noteLabel")` line in place with no remaining use, which fails to compile ('declared and not used: label', verified with go build); the write-up does openly flag that entity substitution capability is being removed and must be hardcoded elsewhere if still needed.

R824.note: DynamicExpresso is an appropriate sandboxed replacement for CSharpScript, but the regex `^[\d+\-*/().\s]+$` rejects any letters at all, so no formula can ever reference the just-registered Total/Tax variables - every real invoice formula fails validation, silently breaking the 'approved formula previews still return a value' contract, and this contradiction is not mentioned.

R825.note: Deleting the billing-scoped CSRF exemption restores default Spring Security CSRF enforcement exactly as the contract requires, with no broadening of any other exclusion.

R826.note: Extension now comes from a map keyed by the already-validated detectedType (matching allowedContentTypes 1:1), so legitimate uploads get the correct extension and attacker-chosen extensions are impossible.

R827.note: Adds length > buffer_len - offset check after the existing offset check (avoiding underflow), matching the contract's fits-entirely-within-buffer_len requirement exactly.

R828.note: Replaces GroovyShell with a context-scoped Commons JEXL evaluator carrying only basePrice/quantity; the fallback-to-basePrice-on-parse-error behavior is a stated, intentional change, not a silent one.

R829.note: Converts to CommandType.StoredProcedure with a bound @customerId parameter, matching the contract's literal-value requirement with no other change to the call or return.

R830.note: Tika-based magic-byte detection correctly replaces trust in the client Content-Type header; the disclosed ImageIO re-encode step changes the stored bytes (recompression, metadata stripped) and would reject legitimate CMYK JPEGs (a known ImageIO limitation) that the original code stored successfully, which isn't mentioned.

R831.note: serializer.save(owner=self.request.user) overrides any client-supplied owner in validated_data (DRF merges save() kwargs last), closing the ownership-spoofing gap with no other observable change.

R832.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode() applied to both interpolated values is correct for the HTML body context and changes nothing else.

R833.note: Alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen allowlist blocks every cmd.exe metacharacter, which correctly sidesteps the .bat-via-cmd.exe re-parsing problem that the offered ArgumentList alternative alone would not fully solve.
